>Yes, you can. LSJ stated about this before. If you play D action on
>yourself, it becomes an undirected action. Want some examples? here they

That's true, but Goth Band's (errata'ed) card text disallows this:

Unique Ally with 2 life. 1 strength, 0 bleed. As a +1 stealth (D)
action, the Goth Band may move one counter from any master card
controlled by another Methuselah to a master card you control that
uses counters. The counter is changed to a counter of the type
appropriate to the new card.

The errata was added to preserve the functionality of Goth Band, which
was designed back when the (D) symbol was errata'ed to prohibit
self-directing (and enabled omni-directing otherwise).

Messages.Author: Emmit Svenson
Messages.Body:
My solution:

Put Succubus Club, Dreams of the Sphinx, Goth Band (Clan Impersonate a
Ravnos to an !Tor; burn the CI after recruiting GB) and Week of
Nightmares in play. Use SC to trade your grandpredator/grandprey ally
Dreams of the Sphinx and the SC. Steal a DoS counter and put it on
WoN. On your ally's turn (and every turn thereafter), trade SC, GB,
WoN and DoS between you so both of you can take turns tapping DoS and
moving its counters to WoN. In a four-player game this can keep both
WoN and DoS going until someone is ousted, and in a 5+ player game
both masters will stick around much longer, maybe long enough to oust
people down to 4. On the downside, your Ravnos will have LOTS of WoN
counters on them, so you'd better use Guard Duty on the SC and hold on
to some Sudden Reversals to keep others from contesting SC and DoS.

'Tis a pity I have no GBs or WoNs.
